questions.text: The SCORES platform was launched by SEBI in:
questions.explanation: SEBI launched the SCORES (SEBI Complaints Redress System) in 2011 to digitize grievance handling.

questions.text: The SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations aim to:
options: Prevent use of unpublished price-sensitive information for trading
questions.explanation: These regulations prohibit trading based on unpublished price-sensitive information to protect market integrity.

questions.text: A bond trades at a premium to face value when:
options: Coupon rate is equal to the current market yield
Coupon rate is higher than the current market yield
Coupon rate is lower than the current market yield
questions.explanation: If the bond’s coupon exceeds the market yield, investors are willing to pay more than face value, so the bond trades at a premium.

questions.text: Which of these is a red flag for a potential debt trap?
options: Using secured loans for asset purchase
questions.explanation: Using new debt to repay old indicates unsustainable leverage.

questions.text: The formula for the Sharpe Ratio is:
options: (Portfolio Return – Risk-Free Rate) / Standard Deviation of Portfolio
questions.explanation: Sharpe Ratio = (Rp – Rf) / σp, where Rp is portfolio return, Rf is risk-free rate, and σp is portfolio’s standard deviation.

questions.text: Which asset class traditionally offers the best protection against inflation over the long term?
questions.explanation: Over long periods, equities have historically outpaced inflation better than most fixed-income instruments, though with higher volatility.

questions.text: Holders of equity shares are known as:
questions.explanation: Equity shareholders are owners and have residual claims on assets and profits.

questions.text: Why is documentation of the financial plan important?
options: To avoid any future changes to the plan
To create a clear record of recommendations, assumptions and responsibilities
questions.explanation: Writing the plan ensures clarity, accountability and provides a reference for future review.

questions.text: Which of the following principles ensures PMS fees are not charged twice for the same performance?
questions.explanation: Under the high-watermark principle, performance fees are charged only when portfolio value exceeds its previous peak.

questions.text: Self-Regulatory Organizations (SROs) in securities markets must:
options: Always act in the best interest of investors and abide by SEBI directions
Have no role in member supervision
questions.explanation: SROs must follow SEBI’s directions, supervise members, and act in the interest of investors.

questions.text: Churning of client portfolios refers to:
options: Rebalancing as per agreed asset allocation
Excessive buying and selling primarily to earn higher fees or commissions
Investing in multiple funds for diversification
Switching from regular to direct plans
questions.explanation: Churning is unethical when trades are executed unnecessarily to generate more brokerage or fees, not to benefit clients.

questions.text: A personal cash-flow statement summarises:
options: Assets and liabilities at a point in time
Income and expenses over a period of time
questions.explanation: It captures inflows and outflows during a period, similar to an income statement.

questions.text: AIFs are primarily targeted at:
questions.explanation: Given the high minimum investment and risk profile, AIFs are intended for sophisticated and high-net-worth investors.

questions.text: The investor’s ultimate record of ownership in mutual funds held in demat form is maintained by:
questions.explanation: In demat mode, the Depository Participant (DP) maintains the record of ownership under the investor’s demat account.

questions.text: The Rule of 72 gives:
options: Exact number of years to double an amount
Approximate years to double money at given rate
Half of the rate of return
questions.explanation: Rule of 72 approximates doubling time = 72 ÷ rate of return.

questions.text: A limit order is an order to:
options: Buy or sell immediately at current market price
Buy or sell at a specified price or better
Buy only if price goes to upper circuit
Sell only at day’s closing price
questions.explanation: Limit orders specify maximum buy or minimum sell price.

questions.text: Tax considerations affect portfolio construction because:
options: Different types of income are taxed differently
Taxes have no impact on net returns
Investors can ignore capital gains tax
questions.explanation: Interest, dividends, and capital gains are taxed differently; hence tax planning affects net portfolio returns.

questions.text: Regulatory constraints are most likely to apply when:
options: The investor wants to invest abroad under LRS limits
The investor invests only in mutual funds
questions.explanation: Under RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), Indian residents can invest up to $250,000 overseas annually—this acts as a regulatory constraint.

questions.text: In mutual fund transactions, the term 'folio number' refers to:
options: Unique identification number for each investor account
questions.explanation: Each investor account with an AMC is assigned a unique folio number for identification and record-keeping.

questions.text: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs is primarily responsible for:
options: Administration of the Companies Act and corporate regulation
questions.explanation: MCA administers the Companies Act, LLP Act and related laws governing corporate entities.

questions.text: SEBI’s main functions are categorized under:
questions.explanation: SEBI performs regulatory, developmental, and protective roles to ensure transparent and efficient capital markets.

questions.text: The Certainty Equivalent Rate (CER) represents:
options: The highest return expected on a risky portfolio
The rate at which a risk-free investment is equally attractive as a risky portfolio
The average of all expected portfolio returns
The minimum guaranteed rate offered by the government
questions.explanation: CER is the rate a risk-free investment must offer to make an investor indifferent between it and a risky portfolio.

questions.text: Lock-in period for investment in an Angel Fund portfolio company is at least:
questions.explanation: Investments by an Angel Fund in a portfolio company must be locked in for a minimum of three years.

questions.text: A change in mode of holding (single to joint) in a mutual fund folio:
options: Is allowed with consent of all parties
Is not permitted; a new folio must be created
questions.explanation: Change in mode of holding is not allowed in existing folios; a new folio must be created with the new configuration.

questions.text: Stock exchanges primarily provide:
options: A platform for trading securities with price discovery and liquidity
questions.explanation: Stock exchanges enable trading, liquidity and transparent price discovery in securities.

questions.text: Effective grievance redress mechanisms help in:
options: Improving investor trust and market integrity
questions.explanation: Robust grievance redress systems improve investor confidence, reduce disputes, and enhance market integrity.

questions.text: A personal balance sheet differs from a cash-flow statement because it shows:
options: A snapshot of assets, liabilities and resulting net worth
questions.explanation: Balance sheet = Assets – Liabilities = Net Worth at a specific date.

questions.text: If monthly income ₹1 lakh and total EMIs ₹35,000, DTI ratio is:
Debt consolidation is a strategy to:
options: Merge multiple loans into one with better terms
questions.explanation: Combining debts reduces complexity and can lower interest burden.

questions.text: Spread risk in credit markets is the risk that:
options: The yield difference between a corporate bond and a government bond of similar maturity widens
The difference between coupon and face value increases
The bid-ask spread in equity markets narrows
questions.explanation: Spread risk is the risk that the credit spread over government securities widens due to perceived higher risk, lowering bond prices.

questions.text: Which of the following complaints is typically NOT handled through SCORES?
questions.explanation: SCORES addresses regulatory or procedural violations; mere dissatisfaction with performance does not qualify.

questions.text: Under SEBI regulations, intermediaries must retain records for a minimum period of:
questions.explanation: SEBI requires intermediaries to maintain client and transaction records for at least five years.

questions.text: Liquid funds invest only in debt and money market securities with residual maturity of:
questions.explanation: Liquid funds invest in debt and money market instruments with maturity of up to 91 days.

questions.text: The main advantage of secured loans over unsecured loans is:
options: Lower interest rates due to collateral
questions.explanation: Collateral reduces lender’s risk, allowing lower interest rates.

questions.text: Portfolio rebalancing frequency should balance between:
options: Market volatility and interest rate movement
Cost of rebalancing and cost of deviation from target
questions.explanation: The decision on rebalancing frequency depends on weighing the cost of rebalancing against the risk of being off-target.

questions.text: Which is an example of good debt?
options: Loan to buy depreciating asset on EMI
questions.explanation: Borrowing for education or business that enhances earning potential is considered good debt.

questions.text: Asset allocation refers to:
options: Choosing individual securities within an asset class
Deciding how to distribute wealth among different asset classes
Timing entry and exit in equity markets
questions.explanation: Asset allocation is the process of dividing an investor’s portfolio among different asset classes such as equity, debt, and cash.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the term financial independence?
options: Having sufficient assets and income sources to maintain desired lifestyle without active employment
questions.explanation: Financial independence means being able to meet living expenses from investments and passive income without needing to work.

questions.text: If volatility of the underlying asset increases, option premiums:
questions.explanation: Higher volatility raises the probability of favourable movement, increasing both call and put option premiums.

questions.text: Expected return of an individual security is calculated as:
options: Sum of potential returns divided by number of outcomes
Sum of possible returns weighted by their respective probabilities
Return on risk-free security plus risk premium
questions.explanation: Expected return is computed by summing potential returns multiplied by their probabilities.

questions.text: The minimum corpus for each AIF scheme must be at least:
questions.explanation: Each AIF scheme must have a minimum corpus of ₹50 crore, while angel funds have relaxed limits.

questions.text: Circuit filters or price bands are imposed to:
options: Prevent extreme price movements in a single day
questions.explanation: Circuit filters cap daily price moves within a band to curb excessive volatility.

questions.text: Liquidity in the stock market means:
options: Ability to trade shares quickly without major price change
questions.explanation: Liquidity allows quick trade execution at stable prices.

questions.text: An option is said to be 'in the money' when:
options: The holder has not paid the premium
The option would yield a positive payoff if exercised immediately
questions.explanation: An in-the-money option has intrinsic value; exercising it immediately would generate a gain for the holder.

questions.text: Under SEBI regulations, investor complaints must be redressed within:
questions.explanation: Intermediaries are expected to resolve investor grievances within 30 days of receipt.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about standard deviation in portfolio theory?
options: It measures the average return of a portfolio
It measures dispersion of returns around the mean
It is always equal to variance
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of variance and measures the dispersion of returns around the mean.

questions.text: Dynamic bond funds:
options: Maintain a fixed portfolio duration at all times
Can move across different durations based on interest rate view
Invest only in government securities of 10-year maturity
questions.explanation: Dynamic bond funds actively manage duration and credit exposure, shifting across maturities according to the fund manager’s interest rate outlook.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers must not accept funds or securities worth less than:
questions.explanation: The minimum threshold of ₹50 lakh applies to each client’s investment under PMS.

questions.text: If a complaint remains unresolved even after arbitration, an investor may approach:
questions.explanation: Investors can approach Consumer Courts or High Courts if dissatisfied after arbitration.

questions.text: A high P/E ratio usually implies that:
options: Investors expect high growth or future earnings potential
questions.explanation: A high P/E often reflects investor optimism about future growth, though it can also indicate overvaluation.

questions.text: If two assets are perfectly positively correlated, diversification will:
options: Have no effect on portfolio risk
questions.explanation: Perfect positive correlation (correlation coefficient = +1) means both assets move identically, offering no diversification benefit.

questions.text: For arbitration of disputes between investors and brokers, the forum used is:
questions.explanation: Exchange arbitration panels handle disputes between investors and brokers as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a lifestyle goal?
options: Owning a bigger car within 3 years
Paying off credit card dues this month
questions.explanation: Lifestyle goals relate to a desired standard of living, such as owning a bigger car or a better house.

questions.text: If an individual saves ₹5,000 per month from ₹1,00,000 income, his annual savings ratio is:
In PMS, fixed cost refers to:
options: A variable charge based on profits
A percentage of assets under management payable regardless of performance
questions.explanation: Fixed cost is the management fee charged as a fixed percentage of AUM irrespective of performance.

questions.text: Which of the following return measures eliminates the effect of external cash flows?
questions.explanation: Time-weighted return neutralizes the impact of deposits and withdrawals, accurately reflecting portfolio manager performance.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines present value?
options: Current equivalent of a future amount discounted at an appropriate rate
Sum of principal and interest earned
questions.explanation: Present value is the amount that needs to be invested today to reach a desired future value, given a rate and time.

questions.text: The financial life cycle typically starts with which stage?
questions.explanation: The financial life cycle begins when an individual starts earning and accumulating assets.

questions.text: The 50-30-20 rule for budgeting suggests allocating:
questions.explanation: A common thumb-rule: 50 % essentials, 30 % discretionary, 20 % savings.

questions.text: In a conservative hybrid fund, the typical allocation to debt and equity is:
questions.explanation: Conservative hybrid funds predominantly invest in debt (75–90%) with a small equity allocation of 10–25%.

questions.text: Why should irregular income (like bonuses) be treated carefully in budgeting?
options: It may not occur regularly and shouldn’t fund fixed commitments
It should always be spent fully
questions.explanation: Irregular income is uncertain and best used for one-time goals or debt reduction.

questions.text: If a client insists on a speculative strategy beyond their risk profile, the adviser should:
options: Accept immediately to earn more fees
Explain risks, document the discussion, and, if still unsuitable, decline or limit the engagement
questions.explanation: Ethically, the adviser must educate, document, and avoid participating in clearly unsuitable strategies.

questions.text: From the perspective of an individual investor, the MOST important trade-off while choosing an asset class is between:
questions.explanation: The core decision is how much risk the investor is willing to take for a particular level of expected return.

questions.text: The full form of SCORES is:
options: Securities Complaint Online Resolution & Evaluation System
Securities Compliance and Oversight Registration System
questions.explanation: SCORES stands for SEBI Complaints Redress System.

questions.text: In the corporate bond ecosystem, the role of a Debenture Trustee (DT) is to:
options: Protect interests of debenture holders and monitor security cover
questions.explanation: Debenture Trustees hold security on behalf of debenture holders and ensure compliance with trust deed and protection of investors’ interests.

questions.text: The KYC process for investors in India is governed by:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates KYC for capital market investors through registered KRAs (KYC Registration Agencies).

questions.text: Which expense would be classified as discretionary?
questions.explanation: Dining out is non-essential and discretionary in nature.

questions.text: The minimum investment amount a client must place with a Portfolio Manager is:
questions.explanation: SEBI regulations stipulate a minimum investment of ₹50 lakh for investors availing PMS.

questions.text: Reinvestment risk is best described as the risk that:
options: Coupons received may have to be reinvested at lower interest rates than initially expected
The issuer may not pay coupons at all
Bond prices will fall when interest rates fall
A bond cannot be sold before maturity
questions.explanation: Reinvestment risk is the risk that future cash flows (coupons or principal) will be reinvested at lower rates, reducing overall realised return.

questions.text: Which channel most directly involves the Registered Investment Adviser (RIA) in the investment decision?
options: Client buying direct equity on their own without advice
Client investing in a mutual fund through a distributor only
Client taking model portfolio advice from an RIA and investing accordingly
Client keeping all money in a savings bank account
questions.explanation: Here, the RIA provides customised advice or model portfolios that the client implements, reflecting the advisory role specified by SEBI’s IA regulations.

questions.text: A closed-end mutual fund scheme:
options: Is generally listed on a stock exchange to provide liquidity
Always allows redemption directly with the AMC
questions.explanation: Closed-end schemes are for a fixed term and are mandatorily listed on a stock exchange so investors can exit by selling units there.

questions.text: Which entity holds the securities and assets of an AIF in custody?
questions.explanation: A registered custodian is mandatory for all Category III AIFs and for Category I and II AIFs with corpus ≥ ₹500 crore.

questions.text: If an investor receives ₹10,000 every year for 5 years, the present value at 8% p.a. is (approx.):
Mutual funds, AIFs and PMS are similar in that they:
options: Are pooled or managed investment vehicles with a defined investment policy
Are only available to retail investors with very small amounts
Can be sold without any regulation
questions.explanation: MFs, AIFs and PMS are managed vehicles that invest according to stated strategies. They differ in structure, regulation and target investors.

questions.text: Mark-to-market in futures trading means:
options: Adjusting contract value daily for changes in market price
Fixing profit at the start of the contract
questions.explanation: Mark-to-market involves daily settlement of profit or loss due to price movement, adjusting each participant’s margin account.

questions.text: Diversification in investments primarily aims to:
options: Spread risk by combining assets that do not move together perfectly
Eliminate all risk from the portfolio
questions.explanation: Diversification reduces unsystematic risk by combining assets whose returns are not perfectly correlated.

questions.text: The nominal rate of interest is 12% p.a. compounded monthly. The effective annual rate (EAR) is closest to:
Find the present value of ₹50,000 receivable after 5 years at 9% p.a. compounded annually.
Which of the following is NOT a type of derivative?
questions.explanation: Equity shares are not derivatives—they are primary financial instruments. Forwards, futures and options are derivatives.

questions.text: An ethical response, if a mistake is made in executing client instructions, is to:
options: Hide the error and hope markets recover
Promptly disclose the error, correct it, and compensate where required
questions.explanation: Honesty and accountability require disclosure of mistakes, corrective action, and fair compensation if client suffers loss.

questions.text: Net Asset Value (NAV) per unit is calculated as:
options: Net assets divided by face value
Number of units divided by net assets
Net assets divided by number of outstanding units
Total investments divided by number of investors
questions.explanation: NAV per unit = Net assets / Number of outstanding units.

questions.text: In goal-based financial planning, investment products are selected:
options: After understanding each goal’s time horizon, risk and amount required
questions.explanation: Products should fit the goal’s characteristics: amount, time horizon and risk tolerance.

questions.text: Setting exposure limits to sectors and asset classes helps to:
questions.explanation: Exposure limits prevent excessive concentration in a single sector or security, reducing portfolio risk.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly lists equity shareholder rights?
options: Voting rights, dividend entitlement, right to information
Only right to capital repayment before others
questions.explanation: Shareholders enjoy voting rights, dividends (if declared), and rights to company information.

questions.text: Complaints related to the National Pension System (NPS) are handled by:
options: PFRDA and the Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA)
questions.explanation: PFRDA and its designated CRA handle NPS-related complaints through their grievance redress mechanism.

questions.text: Under SEBI rules, portfolio managers cannot make investments in:
questions.explanation: SEBI prohibits PMS from investing in below-investment-grade securities to protect investors.

questions.text: Portfolio optimization requires estimation of which parameters?
options: Expected returns, standard deviations, and correlation coefficients
questions.explanation: Portfolio optimization requires estimates of expected returns, risk (standard deviation), and correlation between securities.

questions.text: Why is it important to prioritise financial goals?
options: Because only one goal can be achieved
Because resources are usually limited and not all goals can be met simultaneously
To avoid investing in equity products
questions.explanation: Most people face resource constraints, so goals must be ranked to allocate savings effectively.

questions.text: The Registrar of Companies (RoC) is responsible for:
options: Registering companies and monitoring compliance with company law
questions.explanation: RoC registers companies and ensures they comply with provisions of the Companies Act.

questions.text: A stock split means:
options: Company merges two shares into one
Company divides each share into smaller units to increase liquidity
Company issues new shares for cash
questions.explanation: A stock split divides shares into smaller units to make them more affordable and increase liquidity.

questions.case_text: Arjun, aged 40, recently lost his job. He has ₹10 lakh in savings, monthly expenses of ₹60,000, and no outstanding loans. His priority is to sustain expenses while searching for new employment.

questions.text: Monthly expenses are:

questions.case_text: Amit and Neha, both aged 30, earn ₹1,00,000 per month jointly. They wish to buy a house worth ₹60 lakh in 5 years and also start saving for retirement at 60. Their current savings are ₹5 lakh invested in bank FDs. They can save ₹25,000 per month. Inflation is 6% p.a.

questions.text: Which of the following is Amit and Neha’s short-term goal?
questions.explanation: Emergency fund (3–6 months expenses) is short-term.

questions.text: Buying the house in 5 years is best categorised as a:
questions.explanation: Goals 3–7 years away are medium-term.

questions.text: Retirement planning is a ______ goal.
questions.explanation: Retirement lies 30 years ahead — a long-term goal.

questions.text: Their total monthly saving rate is:
To beat inflation over long term, they should allocate more to:
questions.explanation: Equities have potential to outperform inflation over long horizons.

questions.case_text: Rohit wants to buy a car costing ₹12 lakh. His bank offers a 5-year loan at 10% p.a. interest. He can pay the full price from his savings or take the loan and invest his money in a debt mutual fund earning 7% p.a.

questions.text: Loan interest rate offered is:

What factor mainly decides his choice?
options: Difference between loan rate and investment return

questions.case_text: Ritika plans to accumulate ₹10 lakh in 8 years for her MBA. She can invest in a debt fund giving 8% p.a. compounded annually.

questions.text: How much must Ritika invest today (approx.)?
If she invests ₹5 lakh today, how much will she have after 8 years?
If the fund compounds quarterly, the effective annual yield will:
questions.explanation: More frequent compounding slightly increases effective yield.

questions.text: Rule of 72 says doubling at 8% takes roughly:
questions.explanation: 72 ÷ 8 ≈ 9 years (approx.).
